children: The U.S. auto safety regulator has concluded its review of a 2022 Honda
recall involving rear-view camera problems in 129,092 Ridgeline pickup trucks, saying further regulatory action was not warranted.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration launched the review in 2024 and moved to a more detailed engineering investigation in February 2025. The escalation followed reports that wiring harnesses had failed in some vehicles even after the original recall repair had been performed, Reuters reported.
NHTSA said its subsequent examination did not substantiate concerns that the repaired harnesses would develop failures.

Investigators at the agency's Vehicle Research and Test Center gathered information from vehicle owners, examined selected trucks and subjected the wiring harnesses to durability testing. They found no instances in which harness damage had caused a rear-view camera failure, NHTSA said.
The regulator also said the component was not expected to experience failure over a reasonable operating life.

Most of the complaints received during the investigation related to other types of rear-view camera or wiring-harness problems, NHTSA said. Those issues could not be tied to the durability concern that prompted the engineering analysis.
The agency has now closed the investigation without recommending additional action.

title: NHTSA ends review of Honda Ridgeline camera recall
